Land Use and Development
Regional
In 1966 the Southeastern Misconsin Regional Planning
Commission (SEMPPC) completed and adopted a comprehensive regional
land use plan and a comprehensive regional transportation plan
for the seven county Southeastern Misconsin Region. This plan included
specific recommendations for the improvement of highway transportation
facilities, and is presently engaged in a continuing, area-wide, connective,
land use-transportation planning process pursuant to the provisions
of the 1962 Federal Aid Highway Act.
From this plan, figure 12 shows the general land usage of the region as it existed in 1963. If the land use development conforms to the forecasts as expressed in the various local land use plans and corresponding zoning codes the land use by 1990 will be as previously shown in figure 6. These land use areas will be served by the region's arterial highway system.
As part of the continuing planning process "ilwaukee County with the help of SEMRPC pursued and adopted a Jurisdictional Highway Plan which designated responsibility for the construction, maintenance, and operation of arterial streets and highways in !!ilwaukee County.
Since the adoption of this plan by the various governmental agencies involved, Milwaukee County has begun implementing arterial street and highway improvements within Milwaukee County. The plan should provide the county with an integrated highway transportation system which would promote desirable land use patterns, abate traffic congestion, reduce accidents and travel times.
